up.note:
An expectational certificate assignment $\{w^x\}$ is, at each $x$, feasible for the
fractional certificate LP up to the product structure:
$\sum_{i: x_i\ne y_i} w^x_i \ge \sum_{i: x_i \ne y_i} w^x_i w^y_i \ge 1$.
The inequality is checked pairwise on $(x,y)$ with $f(x)\ne f(y)$, and restricting
to a domain only removes constraints from both LPs, so it survives to partial $f$.

A single character has sparsity $1$ and $\mathrm{osss} = 1$: the two agree, but neither
grows, so this witnesses no exponent. No function in the zoo has $\mathrm{osss}$ growing
while $\mathrm{spar}$ stays bounded -- indeed $\mathrm{spar}(f) = O(1)$ forces $f$ to be a
constant-size combination of characters, and $\mathrm{osss}$ is then bounded too.
